chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sulaymān al-Jaʿfarī, who said:
I saw Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام saying to his son al-Qāsim:
“Rise, my son, and recite at the head of your brother
until you complete it.” So he recited, and when he reached
‘Are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?’

the young man passed away. Then when he was covered and they had gone out, Yaʿqūb ibn Jaʿfar approached him and said to him: “We used to know that when death came upon the dying person, we would recite near him
So now you are commanding us to recite al-Ṣāffāt?” He said: “My son, it is never recited near one in distress except that Allah hastens his relief.”

key_terms.عِنْدَ رَأْسِ: at the head side of the dying person
key_terms.مَكْرُوبٍ: one afflicted with distress or agony
key_terms.وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا: the opening verse of Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt, instructed for recitation here
key_terms.يس وَالْقُرْآنِ الْحَكِيمِ: the opening of Sūrat Yā Sīn, mentioned as a known recitation for the dying

ai.seo_question: What should be recited near a dying person according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructed that Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt be recited beside a dying young man, and the young man passed away during its recitation. When asked about this practice in place of reciting Sūrat Yā Sīn, the Imam عليه السلام said that reciting it near one in distress brings swift relief from Allah.
